alt: Two columns. In Makkah: persecution, the boycott of Banu Hashim, the Year of Sorrow, loss of Abu Talib’s protection and rejection at Ta’if. In Yathrib, to the north: an oasis divided between the Aws and the Khazraj, also home to Jewish tribes, which could offer a place to worship freely.
caption: Makkah had become unsafe; Yathrib offered a place to live as a community.

alt: Three steps: first contact with a small group from the Khazraj; the first pledge of Aqaba by twelve men about belief and conduct, after which Mus’ab ibn Umair (RA) taught in Yathrib; and the second pledge by more than seventy men and two women to protect the Prophet (pbuh). A note gives the importance of the pledges.
caption: The first pledge was about belief and conduct; the second added protection.

alt: The Quraysh plot to strike together, then two columns. Hazrat Ali (RA) slept in the Prophet’s bed and stayed to return the goods held in trust before walking to Madinah. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) prepared camels and a guide, left by night heading south and hid in the Cave of Thawr, helped by his family.
caption: Ali (RA) had two roles: he slept in the bed and returned the trusts.

alt: Six steps of the journey: leaving Makkah by night heading south, three days in the Cave of Thawr, Suraqa ibn Malik turning back, arrival at Quba in 622 CE and founding the first mosque, the first Jummah prayer, and arrival in Madinah where al-Qaswa knelt on land the Prophet (pbuh) paid for.
caption: The Prophet (pbuh) did not go straight to Madinah: Thawr and Quba came first.

alt: Two columns comparing the Mosque of Quba, the first mosque in Islam, founded in 622 CE and linked by many scholars to Qur’an 9:108, with Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah, built of mud brick and palm with a suffah, and used for teaching, judging and planning. A note gives the lesson of 9:107–108.
caption: Quba came first; the Prophet’s Mosque became the centre of the community.

alt: Six terms of the Charter of Madinah, each linked to what it achieved: one Ummah ending the Aws and Khazraj conflict, religious freedom for Jewish tribes, shared defence, justice above tribal loyalty, disputes referred to Allah and the Prophet (pbuh), and Madinah as a protected area.
caption: Describe each term with the problem it solved.

alt: Each Muhajir, a migrant who had lost everything, was paired as a brother with an Ansari helper from Madinah to share homes, work and property. Example: Sa’d ibn al-Rabi’ (RA) offered half his wealth to Abdur Rahman ibn Awf (RA), who asked only to be shown the market.
caption: The brotherhood solved a social and economic crisis without conflict.
